petrov-defence::1::Nxf7@10.say: Nxf7 — the Cochrane sacrifice in the 3.d4 line. Take it: Kxf7, a clean piece up for a pawn. Now the only task is safety — …d5 shuts the diagonal, the king tucks to g8, and the extra piece decides. Don't panic, don't grab.

petrov-defence::3::Bd3@10.say: Bd3 eyes your king down the b1-h7 road, but you're a whole piece up — just keep tidying. With …d5 already blunting the diagonal, walk the king to g8 behind …Re8 and the material simply wins. The bishop barks; it cannot bite.
petrov-defence::3::Bd3@10.short: Bd3 — tuck the king to g8.

petrov-defence::3::Bd3@12.say: Bd3 aims at your king, calmly parried. A piece up with …Re8 already in, walk the king to g8 and untangle with …Nf6 and …c6. White has a bishop pointed at granite and nothing behind it.

petrov-defence::3::d5@14.say: d5 jabs your e6-bishop — a tempo, nothing more. Slide it back to f5 or g4, the king is already safe behind …Re8, and your extra piece carries the game. White is just spending moves he can't afford.
petrov-defence::3::d5@14.short: d5 — retreat the bishop, stay up.

petrov-defence::3::f4@12.say: f4 grabs kingside space, but with no pieces behind it the storm is bluster. Strike back with …d5 in the centre, walk the king to g8, and your extra piece overwhelms a lone pawn-push.

petrov-defence::3::Bg5@12.say: Bg5 pins your f6-knight against the queen — shrug it off with …h6. After Bxf6 Bxf6 you've traded into a clean, safe extra piece; tuck the king to g8 and convert at your leisure.

petrov-defence::3::Be2@12.say: Be2 — a meek developing move that does nothing to your fortress. You're a piece up; finish the job with …Kg8, …c6 and …Nbd7, and the material tells with no counterplay in sight.

petrov-defence::3::Qe2@14.say: Qe2 lines the queen up behind the bishop's old diagonal — but you've already blunted it with …Be6. A piece up, walk the king to g8, offer the light-bishop trade, and convert the extra piece.
petrov-defence::3::Qe2@14.short: Qe2 — king to g8, trade down.

petrov-defence::3::Nc3@8.say: Nc3 develops, but without the d4-and-Bc4 pressure White has even less for the piece. Plant …Be6 to guard the light squares, roll …d5, walk the king home, and the extra piece is decisive.
